query: Which open-source agent frameworks gained the most production adoption this year, and what do independent (non-vendor) sources say about where each breaks down at scale?
scope_constraints: Open-source agent frameworks only: public repository plus a recognized open-source license; closed or proprietary-only platforms are out of scope
'This year' is interpreted as the trailing 12 months ending at the run date (2025-10 through 2026-10); the report states this window explicitly
Break-down-at-scale claims must come from independent (non-vendor) sources — vendor documentation may characterize limits but cannot satisfy this obligation alone
Adoption is measured only through public signals (downloads, contributors, star growth, named production case studies); no private usage data exists to check
Exhaustive coverage of every open-source agent framework is not promised: the run ranks the most-adopted candidates it can evidence and reports the rest as gaps

research_questions.question: Which open-source agent frameworks form the current (2026) candidate set from which 'most production adoption' can be measured?
success_criteria: At least 5 named open-source agent frameworks, each with a public repository URL and license recorded
Each named framework has commits or a release within the trailing 12 months (maintenance check)
At least one independent (non-vendor) 2025-2026 source naming the leading frameworks is recorded

research_questions.question: For each shortlisted framework, what do public adoption signals show over the trailing 12 months — downloads, contributors, star growth, and named production use?
success_criteria: At least 2 dated, quantitative adoption signals per shortlisted framework, each with a source URL (registry stats page, repository page, or named production case study)
Usage signals (downloads, production case studies) distinguished from mindshare signals (stars, rankings) in the recorded evidence

research_questions.question: Which frameworks rank as having gained the most production adoption this year, and where do the adoption signals disagree with each other?
success_criteria: A ranked top-3 to top-5 with every rank traceable to recorded RQ2 signals (no rank from memory)
Signal disagreements recorded where they occur (e.g., star growth without download growth), with both sources cited

research_questions.question: What do independent (non-vendor) sources say about where each top-ranked framework breaks down at scale in production?
success_criteria: At least 1 independent source per top-5 framework naming a specific scale limit (concurrency/orchestration, state and memory, observability, cost, team workflow), with the limiting passage quoted or closely paraphrased plus URL and date
Each source's independence from the framework vendor is recorded (engineering postmortem, practitioner thread, benchmark study, or third-party analysis)

research_questions.question: What caveats bound the conclusion — where is independent evidence missing or thin, and what would change the ranking?
success_criteria: Per-framework evidence gaps recorded for any top-5 framework lacking an independent scale account
A stated list of what this run does not establish (e.g., no private deployment data, single-snapshot adoption window)

queries: best open-source AI agent frameworks 2026 comparison
most popular AI agent frameworks 2025 2026 production adoption
per-candidate registry lookups: PyPI/npm download statistics page for each RQ1 framework (pypistats.org, npmjs.com, pepy.tech)
per-candidate repository lookups: GitHub stars, contributors, last-commit page for each RQ1 framework
named production deployments: '<framework> production case study 2025 2026' for each shortlisted framework
no new search — rank from RQ1/RQ2 recorded evidence; re-open an already-surfaced page only if a signal needs verification
practitioner accounts per top-5 framework: '<framework>' at scale OR in production limitations OR lessons learned (engineering blogs, postmortems)
community practitioner threads per top-5 framework: Hacker News or Reddit '<framework>' production pain points 2025 2026
no new search — gaps compiled from RQ1-RQ4 evidence records

required_evidence: Candidate set of at least 5 maintained open-source agent frameworks named by at least one independent 2025-2026 source
At least 2 dated adoption signals with source URLs per shortlisted framework (registry or repository stats, named production case studies)
A ranked top-3 to top-5 in which every rank traces to recorded signals
At least 1 independent (non-vendor) scale-limit account per top-5 framework, with limiting passage and date
Recorded gaps: frameworks dropped for missing evidence, and scale claims that only vendor sources support
